clue.text: England seamer, picked for XI, admits he bowled wide

parts.note: Stuart Broad, the England seam bowler

indicators.note: the phrase for being in the side lets other letters in, so it wraps round them

parts.note: a player picked for the eleven is in the team
taken as written
B is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for bowled

explanation.surface: A cricket report: an England fast bowler, chosen for the side, confesses he sent down a wide.
explanation.walkthrough: 'admits' wraps the team phrase round the pronoun and the bowled letter. Stuart Broad was an England seam bowler; 'wide', a cricket term in the surface, is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Broad in the beam is an idiom for having wide hips, as a ship broad at its widest part.

clue.text: Explosion killing head of Russian administrative region

indicators.note: killing the head means the first letter of the region's word is dropped

parts.note: an oblast is a province in Russia

explanation.surface: A news item: a blast kills the governor of a Russian province.
explanation.walkthrough: 'killing head of' removes the O from OBLAST. An oblast is a Russian (or Ukrainian) administrative province.
explanation.definitionFit: A blast is a sudden violent detonation, a plain synonym for an explosion.

clue.text: Unlimited local drink ban for music maker

indicators.note: without limits, each of the three words loses its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A town bans drinking without limit, and someone protests with a tune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unlimited' strips the outer letters from local, drink and ban, leaving OCA, RIN and A.
explanation.definitionFit: An ocarina is a small egg-shaped wind instrument, an example of something that produces music.

clue.text: Rubbish runs through part of ship

indicators.note: the letter runs through the middle of the ship's word, so it goes inside it

parts.note: a deck is a floor level of a ship
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: Junk is strewn across one section of a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'through' puts R inside DECK.
explanation.definitionFit: Dreck is a Yiddish-derived slang word for worthless trash or junk.

clue.text: Price to pay for wicked mineral deposits found in Northern Territory?

indicators.note: the deposits are found inside the territory, so they sit within its abbreviation

parts.note: NT is the abbreviation for Australia's Northern Territory
ores are rock deposits from which minerals are extracted

explanation.surface: A mining story: a penalty is paid over immoral ore finds in the Australian outback.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found in' places the deposits inside the territory. The definition leans on the saying 'no rest for the wicked'.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb says there is no rest for the wicked, so constant toil is the penalty wrongdoers suffer.

clue.text: A blow in the face?

parts.note: read as a punch to the face, but a blow is also a gust of wind meeting you head-on

explanation.walkthrough: 'Blow' suggests a punch; here it is a wind that blows straight into your face as you travel.
explanation.definitionFit: A wind blowing against your direction of travel strikes you full in the face.

clue.text: Supports Conservative, character-building stuff!

parts.note: to back someone is to support them
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A political slogan: backing the Conservatives builds character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Character-building' sounds like moral improvement but means building a fictional character's history.
explanation.definitionFit: A backstory is the invented past given to a fictional figure, material that fleshes out who they are.

clue.text: Fatty Arbuckle's debut surprisingly poised

indicators.note: a debut is a first appearance, so only the opening letter of the name is used
the letters of the next word turn up in an unexpected order

explanation.surface: Silent film comic Fatty Arbuckle made a surprisingly composed first appearance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fatty' looks like part of the name Fatty Arbuckle but is the definition. 'surprisingly' rearranges POISED to DIPOSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Adipose is the anatomical term for tissue made of or storing fat.

clue.text: Pens text setting out immediate future plan

indicators.note: setting out the letters lays them in a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone writes a message laying out what they will do shortly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setting out' rearranges the letters of PENS TEXT.
explanation.definitionFit: The next step is the following action in a sequence, the move one intends to make soon.

clue.text: Inept, boring team at Euros

indicators.note: boring into the words drills down to the letters inside them

explanation.surface: A dull, incompetent side at the European football championships.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boring' looks like a criticism of the team but says the answer lies within 'team at Euros'.
explanation.definitionFit: Amateur as an adjective means unskilful or unprofessional, close to incompetent.

clue.text: Records military music — Knut's missing the intro!

definitions.note: plural noun for a collection; an archive is a body of records

indicators.note: missing its opening means the first letter of the tune's name is lost

parts.note: a march is music for soldiers to walk in step to
Knut is the setter, so 'Knut's' (Knut has) becomes I've

explanation.surface: Knut has recordings of army band music but is missing the opening bars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing the intro' drops the M of MARCH. The setter's name stands for I, so 'Knut's' is I'VE.
explanation.definitionFit: An archive is a stored collection of documents or files, the historical records of a body.

clue.text: Relative density expressed as 2x2x4?

definitions.meaning: density here means stupidity, compared to something
two-by-four timber boards, a pair of them, shown as 2x2x4

explanation.walkthrough: 'Relative density' sounds like physics but means comparative stupidity; 2x2x4 reads as two lengths of two-by-four timber.
explanation.definitionFit: Thick as two short planks is a British idiom for very stupid, with dense boards as the comparison.

clue.text: See 11
Editor intervened in recycling staple basis for column

indicators.note: the abbreviation comes between letters of the rearranged word
recycling reworks the material of the word into a new form

explanation.surface: An editor stepped in while staples were being recycled before a newspaper column went out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recycling' turns STAPLE into PESTAL, and 'intervened in' puts ED inside it. 'Column' is an architectural pillar, not a newspaper feature.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedestal is the base on which a pillar or statue stands.

clue.text: Main man on board overseeing new IT biz offering unwanted advice

indicators.note: the chess piece's word watches over the other letters by surrounding them

parts.note: the king is the key piece on a chessboard

indicators.note: the letters of 'IT biz' are made new by rearranging them

explanation.surface: The boss in the boardroom supervises a fresh tech venture while lecturing everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Board' suggests a company board; it is a chessboard. 'new' rearranges the letters of 'IT biz', and 'overseeing' wraps the chess piece round them.
explanation.definitionFit: To kibitz is to look on at a game or task and offer unsolicited comments.

clue.text: Rude, skint Victor is leaving

indicators.note: the letter departs, so it is taken out of the word

parts.note: skint is British slang for having no money, so insolvent
Victor is V in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Broke and impolite, Victor is walking out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is leaving' removes V from INSOLVENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Insolent means disrespectfully impertinent, a synonym of rude.

clue.text: Dad later lets it own goal; it makes you sick

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father

indicators.note: the word for later lets the goal abbreviation in, so it surrounds it

parts.note: then means afterwards
OG is the football abbreviation for an own goal

explanation.surface: A father later concedes an own goal, which is sickening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lets' means the word for later lets the goal abbreviation in; 'it' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A pathogen is a micro-organism such as a bacterium or virus that causes disease.

clue.text: Bum absolutely exhausted, no space

parts.note: dead as an adverb means completely, as in dead right
beat is informal for tired out

explanation.surface: A vagrant, utterly worn out with nowhere to sleep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dead beat' means absolutely exhausted; 'no space' says to write it as one word.
explanation.definitionFit: A deadbeat is an idle, feckless person, and bum is American slang for such a loafer.

clue.text: Sweet sherry lovingly delivered?

definitions.meaning: a musical direction to play tenderly

explanation.walkthrough: 'Delivered' means performed, as music is; amoroso is the Italian instruction to play lovingly.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are recorded: a sweet sherry style and the musical marking for an affectionate performance.

clue.text: Hospital returned bunch of flowers containing small leaves

definitions.note: plural for the herb, whose leaves are used in cooking and medicine

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

indicators.note: returned means the flower word, with its extra letter, is read back to front
the bouquet's word holds the abbreviation within it

parts.note: a posy is a small bouquet
S is the abbreviation for small, as in clothing sizes

explanation.surface: Flowers sent back from a hospital had little foliage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'containing' puts S in POSY, and 'returned' reverses POSSY to YSSOP after H.
explanation.definitionFit: Hyssop is an aromatic herb grown for its bitter leaves, an example of a plant used as foliage.

clue.text: Sign southern firm beginning to outperform, coping with a measure of inflation

indicators.note: the business is coping with, holding on to, the inflation measure within its letters

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

parts.note: RPI is the Retail Price Index, a UK measure of inflation

explanation.surface: A sign that a company in the south is starting to do well despite inflation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coping with' puts the inflation measure inside the other letters. The Retail Price Index is Britain's long-standing measure of inflation.
explanation.definitionFit: Scorpio is one of the twelve signs of the zodiac.

clue.text: Miserable individual with retired children

explanation.surface: An unhappy pensioner and their offspring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retired' looks like an instruction to reverse; it is the abbreviation RET.
explanation.definitionFit: A wretch is an unhappy or unfortunate person.

clue.text: Shh! Posh rock star is playing surprise smash hit

indicators.note: a performer playing around with the letters puts them in a new order

explanation.surface: Quiet please: a well-to-do rock musician is performing an unexpected chart-topper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is playing' rearranges SHH POSH ROCK STAR. 'Smash hit' is not a song but a sudden blow.
explanation.definitionFit: A short, sharp shock is a brief harsh punishment or jolt, like an unexpected heavy blow.

clue.text: Close! Hamilton finally involved in car crash

indicators.note: that letter becomes involved in the word for close, sitting inside it

parts.note: shut means close, as an order

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of the driver's name

explanation.surface: A near miss as Lewis Hamilton is caught up in a racing accident.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved in' puts N, the last of Hamilton, inside SHUT. Lewis Hamilton is the Formula One champion.
explanation.definitionFit: Shunt is British motor-racing slang for a collision, especially a minor one.

clue.text: Upper-class quietly shunning sauce boat

indicators.note: the sauce shuns those letters, so they are left out of it

parts.note: ketchup is a tomato sauce
P is piano, the musical marking for quietly

explanation.surface: Posh people discreetly avoid the gravy boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shunning' removes U and P from KETCHUP. 'Sauce boat' reads as one dish; 'sauce' and 'boat' have separate jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: A ketch is a two-masted sailing vessel.

clue.text: Absolutely loving adult party group

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for adult, as in film certificates
a do is an informal word for a party
a ring is a group, such as a gang

explanation.surface: Delighted with a grown-ups' party crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: Adoring means feeling deep affection, a stronger form of loving.

clue.text: Announce PM's retired in utter shambles

indicators.note: the reversed letters sit inside the rearranged word
a shambles is a mess, so the letters are jumbled
retired means going backwards, so the letters of PM are read in reverse

explanation.surface: Declaring that the Prime Minister has stepped down amid total chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shambles' rearranges utter to TRUET, 'retired' reverses the PM letters, and 'in' places them inside the jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: To trumpet is to proclaim loudly, as heralds once did with trumpets.

clue.text: Getting old, like Bugs Bunny?

definitions.meaning: elderly, from horses' gums receding with age
the cartoon rabbit has prominent long front teeth

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading takes the idiom literally: Bugs Bunny's buck teeth are long.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom refers to ageing, as a horse's teeth appear longer when its gums recede.
